source.title: An optimization and generalization analysis for max-pooling networks

record.file_problem: none; full paper text supplied, including appendix
record.tranche_reason: The paper theoretically analyzes optimization and generalization for an overparameterized max-pooling CNN on a specified pattern-detection distribution and empirically compares it with fully connected networks. These results conceptually test V3, using a simplified task and architecture rather than the named image benchmarks and comparisons.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own generalization guarantee, empirical test-error comparisons, and test-error change as the number of patterns varies. The cited results from other work and plot-only values are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out error of a max-pooling CNN and a parameter-matched fully connected network on synthetic pattern-detection tasks and an MNIST digit-composition task. These test V3 in new settings; the theoretical CNN guarantee alone does not establish a CNN–FCN performance separation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate: the authors prove optimization and generalization guarantees for a max-pooling CNN on their constructed distribution and empirically observe a CNN advantage over FCNs, including extensions with noise and MNIST patterns. Their theoretical bound comparison suggests, but does not prove, an actual CNN–FCN performance separation.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical analysis uses a layerwise gradient-descent algorithm and a specially constructed pattern-detection distribution; experiments compare ConvPool, an MLP, and SVM, with standard Adam training for ConvPool. The paper tests a simplified setting rather than the broad image benchmarks in V3.
record.method_sensitivity: Test performance varies with the number of patterns per image: ConvPool is only mildly affected, while MLP and SVM deteriorate. Results are also reported separately for clean toy data, noisy toy data, and an MNIST detection task.

fits_no_version.finding: Layerwise training of the overparameterized pooling CNN has a high-probability test-error guarantee of O(sqrt(d/m)) under the specified distribution and initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overparameterized max-pooling CNNs can have width-independent generalization guarantees on an orthogonal pattern-detection distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: Proposition 6.1 makes the applied FCN margin-based sample-complexity bound scale as O(n^2), versus the CNN's O(d) guarantee. The authors explicitly lack an FCN performance lower bound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These particular generalization guarantees scale more favorably for the CNN; their difference does not prove an actual performance separation.

fits_no_version.finding: ConvPool also outperforms a linear SVM, whose performance deteriorates with added noise and increasing pattern count.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convolution and max pooling improve generalization relative to a linear classifier on these pattern-detection tasks.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence
record.problems: The theoretical guarantee depends on a specially constructed distribution with orthogonal patterns and a layerwise optimizer. The experiments use a constructed detection task and an MNIST detection task, not standard image classification benchmarks. The actual test-error values in the figures are not present in the supplied text; comparisons are stated qualitatively. The authors note that they do not provide a lower bound for FCNs on the distribution.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Numeric test-error values and plotted means/stds are not recoverable from the supplied text, so figure-only values are recorded as such.

untested.parts: Matched training experiments on fixed random labels and natural labels, including held-out chance performance for random labels.
Whether widening beyond interpolation keeps lowering test error; a width-independent bound does not measure this trend.
Standard image-classification benchmarks; the contribution of local connectivity separately from weight sharing and max pooling; learned sparse local connections; initialization from trained CNNs.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizer comparisons and tuning-dependent differences.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V3. Restricted task coverage and unavailable numerical figure values are evidence limitations, not conditions showing that V3 fails; the record's limits_scope label is unwarranted. Qualitative states follow explicit statements in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence are not tested.
No width sweep beyond interpolation or double-descent test-error measurement.

The theory concerns an idealized pattern-detection distribution; empirical evidence uses that distribution, a noisy variant, and an MNIST detection task. It does not test CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, or SVHN, learned sparse connections, or FC networks initialized from trained convolutional networks. The reported figure values are not numerically recoverable from the text.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison; Adam is used for reported ConvPool experiments.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap measure.
